keySentence: Privilege is not permanent — those who define themselves by it lose everything when it goes.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: By the end of Sara's time at Miss Minchin's school something had become impossible to ignore. Sara had lost every material thing and emerged kinder, stronger, and more fully herself. Lavinia had kept all her privilege and yet seemed somehow smaller and less certain inside. The cruelty she had shown Sara had revealed the deep insecurity that privilege had been hiding. She had needed to put Sara down because she had nothing of her own strong enough to stand upon. Sara had never used privilege as a weapon because she had always had something far more lasting. She had her character — built carefully over years and impossible for anyone else to take away. Privilege is not permanent — those who define themselves by it lose everything when it goes.
